subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom yielding glob traversal and allow unrelated event-loop work between sequential `agent:bootstrap` hook handlers as the permanent bootstrap runtime behavior?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well-tested, but it replaces dependency-owned glob semantics and introduces a new scheduling boundary in a session-context mutation path; only the relevant runtime owners can accept those compatibility and interleaving tradeoffs.

options.title: Accept the exact-head design
options.body: Approve the custom parity-tested walker and bootstrap-only handler yields, then require an exact-head live Gateway/channel latency check before merge.

options.title: Land file loading only
options.body: Keep asynchronous guarded reads and timing diagnostics but defer custom glob traversal and hook interleaving to narrower follow-up work.

options.title: Pause the branch
options.body: Do not merge this large runtime change if maintainers are unwilling to own the remaining compatibility and scheduling surface.

recommendation.title: Accept the exact-head design
recommendation.body: Approve the custom parity-tested walker and bootstrap-only handler yields, then require an exact-head live Gateway/channel latency check before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest merged history across the workspace bootstrap, hook, boundary-read, and embedded-run surfaces and merged the original glob capability.
